answer: Continuous Location Attestation. Each agent must answer a challenge routed through a local beacon tied to its physical site, and its reply is signed with a key sealed inside a tamper-resistant module bound to that beacon's clock drift and radio fingerprint. The atlas of enrolled beacons records these signatures, and any identity claiming a meadow site must match drift and fingerprint within tight bounds. A single operator cannot fake drift across many simultaneous sites, since each forged lotus identity needs a distinct physical module, so per-identity cost is one module plus site access,
